items.text: Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in the Nov 3 midterms, according to network projections. CBS projects at least 54 Democratic Senate seats. Reported Senate flips include Texas (Talarico over Paxton), Kansas, Iowa, Ohio, Maine and North Carolina. House races were still being counted.
items.notes: Results are projections, and outlets' House totals differ (CBS projects 251–268 Democratic seats). The defeated South Carolina Republican's name appears garbled in some outlets, so it is left out. CNBC pages would not load.

items.text: The Mississippi and Alaska Senate races were still too close to call on Nov 5. In Mississippi, Democrat Scott Colom led Sen. Hyde-Smith by about 1,100 votes with 96% counted. In Alaska, Mary Peltola led Sen. Sullivan by about 640 votes, with ranked-choice tabulation still to come.
items.notes: Mississippi has no formal recount process, so a legal fight is possible.

items.text: Speaker Mike Johnson will not seek the post of House Republican leader in the next Congress. Scalise and Jordan are reported to be running, and the vote is reportedly set for Nov 10. Jeffries has launched his bid for Speaker, and Schumer says he will be majority leader.

Vice President Vance wrote that Republicans lost because of the Iran war. Trump called that largely true because of gasoline prices, but said he would go to war again, and also blamed weak candidates.
items.notes: Framing differs. Fox describes Republicans as soul-searching, citing Cruz on prices, tariffs and the war. NBC and the Washington Post frame the result as a rejection of Trump. The Washington Post is paywalled.

items.text: The lame-duck Congress returns on Nov 9 facing a Dec 11 government-funding deadline. Also pending are the NDAA, a possible debt-limit increase and HHS confirmations, which Republicans want done before they lose the Senate on Jan 3.

The US and Iran remain far apart. Qatar is seeking backing for a draft that starts with three days of confidence-building steps, while Iran wants the blockade and sanctions lifted before it reopens Hormuz. Axios reports a US strike on Qeshm Island on Nov 3, and Trump says he is in 'no rush' to resume strikes.
Iran's IRGC said two tankers and a tug caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz, one after hitting a mine, after they used 'unauthorised' routes. This has not been independently verified.
The Dow jumped about 1,570 points on Nov 4 and Brent fell about 8%, to the mid-$90s. On Nov 5 chip stocks sold off (AMD −13%, Nvidia −7%) on fears of tougher AI rules under a Democratic Congress.
items.notes: Intraday figures; index levels differed between sources.

items.text: Challenger counted 43,994 announced US job cuts in October, slightly more than September but 71% fewer than a year earlier.
Voters in Washington and Arizona approved measures restricting transgender athletes in girls' sports, with about 56% and 58%, Fox reports. Roughly 160 statewide measures were on ballots nationwide.

The FDA announced several recalls. Evergreen Fresh broccoli sprouts are linked to a Salmonella outbreak (34 ill in six states; CDC says it is over), Once Upon a Farm toddler bars pose a choking risk, and Brad's kale chips may contain thallium.
The Supreme Court's November sitting continued with argument in Guerrero v. Johnson (25-1003).

The CDC's Ebola attestation order took effect at 11:59pm EST on Nov 3. Every international air passenger must attest they have not been in DR Congo in the past 21 days, and separate entry suspensions for DRC, Uganda and South Sudan run to Nov 10.
